## Statement

The **Chebyshev inequality** bounds the probability that a random variable
deviates from its mean by a given amount, in terms of its variance. It follows
directly from the [[markov-inequality]] and is the key tool in the proof of the
weak and strong [[law-of-large-numbers]].

:::{.theorem data-title="Chebyshev's Inequality"}

Let $X$ be a random variable with finite mean $\mathbb{E}X<\infty$ and finite
variance $\operatorname{Var}(X)<\infty$. Then for every $\epsilon>0$
$$
\mathbb{P}(|X-\mathbb{E}X|\geq \epsilon )\leq {\frac{\operatorname{Var}(X)}{\epsilon ^2}}.
$$

:::

:::{.proof}

Apply the [[markov-inequality]] to the non-negative random variable
$(X-\mathbb{E}X)^2$ and the level $\epsilon^2$:
$$
\mathbb{P}(|X-\mathbb{E}X|\geq \epsilon )=\mathbb{P}((X-\mathbb{E}X)^2\geq \epsilon ^2)\leq \frac{\mathbb{E}[(X-\mathbb{E}X)^2]}{\epsilon ^2}=\frac{\operatorname{Var}(X)}{\epsilon ^2}.
$$

:::

If $\operatorname{Var}(X)=\infty$ the bound is trivially true, so only the finite
mean is really needed.
